note: The entry follows Holmgren's 1910 original description (queen and soldier). The original is a library OCR text of a BHL scan (Zenodo/Plazi mirror); the German original description was read line by line; figures that the OCR scrambled beyond confirmation are not listed.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: (The original describes only the queen.) Colour paler than in Eutermes major, from which it differs in the intermediate muscle scars not coalescing with one another but only converging backwards; the posterior margin of the pronotum deeply concave; the mesonotal concavity broader than that of the metanotum. The body length, head length and head width are scrambled in the OCR and not listed.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Almost entirely similar to the soldier of Eutermes major, but the antennae 13-segmented: segment 3 far longer than segment 2 yet less than twice as long; segment 4 equal to segment 2. The groove on the back of the head is almost only a trace. The brown of the head and nasus paler. Head length 1.7—1.95 mm (the mode is printed in the original as '1.5—1.35', evidently OCR damage, so it is not listed); head width 1.05—1.3 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The original records the worker as identical with that of Eutermes major (no separate description).

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The original was published as Eutermes 13-articulatus n. sp. (the specific name meaning 'thirteen-segmented'); figure 37 shows the queen's head. The type locality is not explicitly recorded in the original.
